title: Water Damage Mitigation Drying Deposit
content:
**Payment desk card — Water Damage Mitigation drying deposit**

A self-pay Water Damage Mitigation job collects a drying deposit from the customer before drying equipment is set.

## Rule
The job must be in authorized status when the drying deposit is collected, and only a self-pay job collects one; the drying deposit is the customer's own payment, made by the customer through the company's secure payment channel, and staff never take card numbers. Drying equipment may be set on a self-pay job only after customer payments posted to the job cover every charge posted to the job plus the drying deposit; insurance-funded jobs collect no drying deposit, because the deductible is collected on the claim file rather than on the job. Customer payments other than the drying deposit remain accepted by credit card, debit card, ACH or check, and every customer payment is posted in full to the one job it names; the drying deposit is taken by debit card, ACH or check only, so no card surcharge arises on it.

On a job carrying pad removal, carpet removal or flood cut lines, the amount collected before drying equipment is set is fixed only after the job carries a debris haul-off line.

On a tier that requires antimicrobial treatment, the amount collected before drying equipment is set on a job carrying pad removal, carpet removal or flood cut lines is not worked out until the job carries an antimicrobial line.

## At a glance
| Point | Rule |
|---|---|
| Job status | authorized |
| Funding source | self-pay only; an insurance-funded job collects no drying deposit |
| Who pays | the customer, personally, through the secure payment channel; staff never take card numbers |
| Tender for the drying deposit | debit card, ACH or check; no card surcharge arises on it |
| Posting | in full, to the one job the payment names |

## Paying through the secure payment channel
`pay_drying_deposit_ee9a2909` is a customer-owned tool: the desk agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it through the company's secure payment channel. On success one customer payment is posted in full to the named job with the chosen tender, a processor confirmation number is issued, and the job's balance due falls by the amount; the customer sees the confirmation number and the new balance.

### Parameters
- `water_job_id` — the reference number of the customer's water mitigation job, which the desk agent reads from the water mitigation job lookup and gives to the customer before the payment.
- `payment_method` — the tender the customer pays with, exactly one of: `credit_card` (a credit card), `debit_card` (a debit card), `ach` (a bank transfer from a checking or savings account) or `check` (a paper or electronic check).
- `amount` — the amount paid in USD, a positive amount with exactly 2 decimal places, already rounded to the cent half up before the call.

### Return
On success the tool returns a text receipt of the form "Payment posted: <amount> USD by <tender> to job <job reference>, confirmation <confirmation number>, payment reference <payment reference>; balance due now <balance> USD.", where the confirmation number is the processor confirmation issued for this payment, the payment reference is the new payment line's reference number and the balance is the job's balance due after the payment. The payment has succeeded when the receipt starts with "Payment posted". A text starting with "Error:" means nothing was paid: the tender was not one of the four listed, the amount was not positive or carried more than 2 decimal places, or no water mitigation job has that reference number.
